meta.title: Research @ IITB
meta.subtitle: A detailed report on research at the institute spanning 2020 to 2026, and its impact across the globe
meta.executive_summary: This report provides a comprehensive overview of research activities at IIT Bombay from 2020 to 2026, highlighting its global impact. It details IIT Bombay's rankings, departments, faculty, patents, publications, and citations. The report delves into research impact across departments, the significance of open access, H-index comparisons, publication mix, and a comparison with other top Indian institutes. It also analyzes research authorship distribution, changes in publication author counts, funded research by department and agencies, and key research topics over several years. Finally, it introduces the IITB Professor Research Database as a tool for exploring faculty expertise.

correlation_academic_rank_research_outpu.title: Output by Academic Rank: Share of Career Publications
key_insights: Faculty dominate: Professors (30,512 publications), Associate Professors (11,354) and Assistant Professors (9,834) together account for 98.5% of the 52,505 publications recorded.
Clear rank gradient: average career output per person falls from 103.4 papers for a Professor to 72.3 for an Associate Professor and 53.2 for an Assistant Professor.

Senior outliers: the single Professor (HAG) has 135 publications and the three Chair Professors have 250 between them, while postdoctoral researchers contribute under 1% because their publication careers are short.

Counts cover each researcher's whole career, not a single window; 51 profiles could not be read and are excluded, and 11 people on adjunct, visiting, library, project and research-scholar designations are grouped as "Other designations".

research_authorship_distribution.title: Research Authorship Distribution: Key Insights
research_authorship_distribution.data_points_description: Distribution of papers by team size across the 21,284 IIT Bombay works (2022-2026) that record an author count. Teams of 2-4 authors form the core with 13,270 papers (62.4%); 1-5 author teams together cover 16,835 papers (79.1%), solo-authored papers number 1,258 (5.9%) and 1,055 papers (5.0%) carry 11 or more authors.
key_findings: Modal team size: 5,189 papers (24.4%) are written by exactly 3 authors, ahead of 2 authors (4,440) and 4 authors (3,641).
Small-team core: papers with 1-5 authors account for 16,835 of 21,284 (79.1%).
Sharp tail: only 1,055 papers (5.0%) reach 11 or more authors, driven by large experimental collaborations.
implications: Collaboration is the default: mean team size is 5.5 authors, or 117,174 authorship slots across 21,290 works.
Large teams stay exceptional: papers with 10 or fewer authors cover 95.0% of the output.
research_authorship_distribution.context: Author counts per paper for IIT Bombay works indexed in OpenAlex, 2022-2026, n = 21,284 of 21,290 works (6 works carry no recorded author count). Queried 1 Oct 2026.

key_research_topics_yearly.title: Key research topics from year 2020
key_research_topics_yearly.summary: Research was heavily focused on foundational science like Photoluminescence and Quantum Dots. AI was present with Deep Learning. Coincided with the onset of the global COVID-19 pandemic.

key_research_topics_yearly.title: Key research topics from year 2021
key_research_topics_yearly.summary: Direct impact of the pandemic seen as 'COVID-19' enters the top 10. Optimization and Deep Learning remain key areas. World grappling with logistical challenges and leveraging technology in response to the crisis.

key_research_topics_yearly.title: Key research topics from year 2022
key_research_topics_yearly.summary: Significant shift as 'Machine Learning' appears for the first time, joining Deep Learning and signaling a broadening AI focus. Microstructure research peaks at #1.

key_research_topics_yearly.title: Key research topics from year 2023
key_research_topics_yearly.summary: Year of AI's explosion. 'Machine Learning' soared to the #1 spot, reflecting public and scientific excitement following the widespread release of advanced generative AI models. Foundational topics like Climate Change remained a high priority.

key_research_topics_yearly.title: Key research topics from year 2024
key_research_topics_yearly.summary: AI trend solidifies with 'Machine Learning' and 'Algorithms' ranking as top priorities. 'COVID-19' drops from the top 10, indicating a shift in global health priorities into a post-pandemic phase.

key_research_topics_yearly.title: Key research topics from year 2025
key_research_topics_yearly.summary: Based on 4,514 IIT Bombay works indexed for 2025. Particle-collision physics, catalytic C-H functionalization, perovskite materials and additive manufacturing head the primary-topic counts, with natural language processing carrying the AI theme forward alongside battery and photovoltaic materials.

International = co-authors in 2 or more countries; domestic = every author based in India across 2 or more institutions; single-institution = every author within IIT Bombay. Queried 1 Oct 2026.

changes_in_publication_author_counts.title: Changes in Publication Author Counts
key_findings: Large teams are gaining: papers with 6 or more authors rose from 18.3% (2020) to 22.3% (2025).
Two to five authors remains the backbone: 77.4% of papers in 2020, easing to 69.6% by 2026.
Solo authorship stays rare: 4.3% (2020) to 5.9% (2025), reaching 9.2% in the partial 2026 data.

top_funded_research_topics_yearly.title: Top funded research topics in year 2020
top_funded_research_topics_yearly.summary: Research funding heavily concentrated in optoelectronics and nanotechnology. 'Photoluminescence' and 'Quantum Dots' were dominant. Early appearance of 'Deep Learning' indicated nascent AI trend.

top_funded_research_topics_yearly.title: Top funded research topics in year 2021
top_funded_research_topics_yearly.summary: Reliability tops the funded topics (12), with India (11), Microstructure (10) and Climate Change (9) just behind. Foundational materials science and AI stay high priority: Deep Learning is fifth (8). New entries such as Remote Sensing (7) and Additive Manufacturing (6) show funding broadening into applied engineering and environmental technologies.

top_funded_research_topics_yearly.title: Top funded research topics in year 2022
top_funded_research_topics_yearly.summary: Reinforced importance of materials science with a significant rise in computational methods. Strong debut of 'Density Functional Theory' (DFT) highlighted investment in simulation and modeling. 'Hydrogen Storage' marked the entry of clean energy technology.

top_funded_research_topics_yearly.title: Top funded research topics in year 2023
top_funded_research_topics_yearly.summary: Environmental issues became the foremost priority with 'Climate Change' rising to #1 (10). Clear emphasis on advanced experimental techniques, with X-ray Diffraction second (9), and Photoluminescence climbing to third (8) after ranking sixth in 2022.

top_funded_research_topics_yearly.title: Top funded research topics in year 2024
top_funded_research_topics_yearly.summary: Machine Learning tops the funded topics (10), ahead of Density Functional Theory (8) and Microstructure (7), with India still a common tag (9). Clean energy stays in the list through Hydrogen Storage (6), while Deep Learning slips to ninth (2).

recommendations: Enhance Global Collaboration Visibility: The top 10 university partners and country-level collaboration shares are now shown, with Monash University (551 joint papers) far ahead of the rest. A world map visualization of collaboration density would complete the picture.

Deep Dive into High-Impact Departments: For departments like Physics, Chemistry, and Electrical Engineering, further detailed reports on their specific research breakthroughs, leading research groups, and flagship projects could be developed.

Promote Open Access Further: Publisher-hosted open access already outperforms closed access on citations (hybrid 8.96 and gold 8.66 against 6.06 for closed), while repository-hosted green copies average only 2.26. IIT Bombay should keep supporting open access publishing and encourage authors to deposit accepted manuscripts, through workshops or funding incentives.

Leverage the Professor Research Database: Actively promote the iitb.irins.org database as a resource for internal and external stakeholders to identify research expertise, fostering potential collaborations and interdisciplinary projects.

Analyze Funding Gaps: The department shares shown are indicative estimates, not published figures. For the departments at the lower end (CL, ES, AE), investigate the reasons and explore strategies to secure more research funding, if deemed strategically important.

Visualize Research Trends Over Time: The Timeline page and the year selector on Publications already show 2020 to 2026 trends for topics and author counts. Longer time-series views for AI/ML, Clean Energy and Materials Science would make the trajectory clearer still.

Develop Case Studies: Create detailed case studies of successful research projects, innovations, or patents that have had a significant global impact, showcasing the practical application of IIT Bombay's research.

internal_funding.title: Institute internal funding for R&D, FY 2024-25

key_insights.government_share: Government agencies funded 59% of the Rs 458.45 crore received from sponsored and consultancy projects in FY 2024-25, about Rs 270.49 crore.
key_insights.industry_share: Indian industry was the largest non-government source at 26%, about Rs 119.20 crore.
key_insights.foreign_share: Foreign sources together contributed 12%, about Rs 55.01 crore: 7% foreign organizations and 5% foreign industry.
key_insights.non_government: Non-government sources (Indian and foreign industry plus other organizations) contributed close to 40% of receipts, as stated in the Annual Report.
key_insights.growth: Total external grants for R&D rose to Rs 471.56 crore in FY 2024-25, 10% above the Rs 428.36 crore received in FY 2023-24.
key_insights.dst: DST remains the single largest strategic partner, with Rs 235.17 crore for BharatGen under NM-ICPS and Rs 589 crore sanctioned for the National Quantum Mission thematic hub in quantum sensing and metrology at IIT Bombay.
key_insights.internal: The Institute released Rs 43 crore of its own money for R&D in FY 2024-25, of which Rs 7 crore was seed and augmented seed grant for new faculty.
